name: MS-70CDR
summary: Main target of ZoomMultistompZDL: about 30 custom effects, NAM and cab loaders and a patch editor, tested on firmware 2.10. Modwerk does not list ZDL effects yet.

firmware.flash: Effects are installed with Zoom Effect Manager 2.3.3 or later over USB; the OS is not modified.
firmware.recovery: Remove the effect in Effect Manager. If a bad effect freezes the pedal at boot, run All Initialize (hold the leftmost knob while powering on), then remove the effect.

sdk.toolchain: TI's C6000 compiler 8.5.0.LTS and ZoomMultistompZDL's linker with Leemuzhko's runtime (own_runtime), so a built effect carries no code from Zoom's effects.

budgets.name: Patch DSP
budgets.note: The DSP cost the pedal adds up per patch: Zoom's 2.10 refuses an effect between 224.4 and 228.4 (measured); MIDISTOMP 2.0 raises the limit to 300.

budgets.name: Effect file
budgets.note: The largest effect file proven to load on the MS-70CDR 2.10.

budgets.name: Code and constants
budgets.note: An effect's .text and .const together: the measured load boundary (Leemuzhko's findings).

research.label: ZoomMultistompZDL
research.note: MIT. ZDL linker, ABI notes, DSP safety rules, effects, NAM/cab template loaders, Web MIDI patch editor, Ziddle emulator tests.

research.label: repeat98/ZoomMultistompZDL
research.note: The upstream reverse-engineered toolchain the project builds on.

research.label: MIDISTOMP
research.note: MIT, by Luca Matturro, and Modwerk's planned base. Custom firmware built from Zoom's MS-70CDR 2.10 for the MS-70CDR, MS-50G and MS-60B; v2.0 (November 2026) raises the patch DSP limit from 225 to 300 and adds parallel routing, a perform mode, a looper and MIDI clock sync.

research.label: Matujuice ZDL effects pack
research.note: MIT. 17 effects for synths and drum machines, built with ZoomMultistompZDL's linker; tested on an MS-60B running MS-50G firmware. The tempo-synced ones need MIDISTOMP.
